Personality: Yanagur is the staunchest defender of steppe tradition, his character brimming with the fiery spirit and directness of a nomad. Valuing honor as his very life and keeping every word he speaks, he always leads from the front on the battlefield with extraordinary courage. Yet he is no far-sighted politician: he acts largely on instinct and impulse, lacking long-term calculation, which makes him somewhat unpredictable in diplomacy. Toward dignitaries who attempt to tempt him into settling down with land and serfs, he responds with utter contempt. Neither cruel nor merciful, in his eyes raiding for the survival of the tribe is a heroic tradition handed down by his ancestors rather than a crime. Reserved and pragmatic by nature, with no interest in squandering wealth, his sole desire is to defend the freedom and dignity of the Karakhergit from horseback, making him a quintessential man of action.
Background: As the young leader of the Karakhergit tribe, Yanagur grew up on the great steppes of Kuruluk. His clan is one of the very few among the Khuzait to refuse settlement and insist on a nomadic way of life. In the face of coercion and enticements from successive Khans seeking to assimilate them, Yanagur's ancestors held fast to the traditions of horseback, an aloof pride that earned them a mixture of envy and scorn from other tribes. Mastering superb archery and horsemanship at a very young age, Yanagur honed his leadership through countless cattle raids and counter-raids. Although he intermarries and trades with other tribes, he steadfastly maintains the independent status of the Karakhergit, refusing to swear fealty to any kingdom. Now twenty-five years old and shouldering the destiny of his entire clan across turbulent Calradia, he is sworn to lead this last nomadic host in defending the glory of their ancestors with arrow and lance, never bowing to the shackles of settled civilization.
